3.text: the Chukchee used necklaces made of small objects strung together.

4.text: I have heard that necklaces of the vertebræ of fish were worn by children.

5.text: One of the dolls I collected had a necklace of tiny stones of irregular form

6.text: tied together on a sinew thread.

7.text: Buttons are little known to the Chukchee, since their garments do not

8.text: require any. Some buttons carved out of ivory are used for clasping belts or

9.text: for buttoning pouches and work-bags (Fig. 191, e, f). They may be com-

10.text: pared to the buttons belonging to the Gilyak, and illustrated by Schrenck.²

11.text: SNOW-GOGGLES. — Snow-goggles of leather and wood (Fig. 192, a, b)

12.text: are used by the Chukchee, the Asiatic Eskimo, the Lamut, and other tribes

13.text: of northeastern Asia. They have narrow slits similar to those in the specimens

14.text: from the American Eskimo. The Lamut sometimes fashion snow-goggles of

15.text: the same shape out of thin sheets of silver hammered out of silver coins.

16.text: Nowadays snow-goggles of Yakut make, covered with a net of horsehair, are

17.text: bought from Russian traders. Glass goggles from civilized countries are also

18.text: eagerly purchased. The Chukchee sometimes imitate European snow-goggles,

19.text: but in place of smoked glass or hair-netting they use round bits of iron pierced
